The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The present appeal is filed by the Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 21.07.2015 in MVC.No.1477/2013 passed by Addl. Senior Civil Judge & CJM, and MACT, Mandya,
for questioning the liability and also seeking reduction of quantum of compensation.

2. Brief facts of the case are that, on 16.12.2013 the minor claimant and his father were coming from their relatives house towards their house in bicycle slowly and cautiously on the left side of the M.C.
Road from Budanur towards Mandya.

When the minor claimant and his father came near Sanjo Hospital at around 7.15 to 7.30 pm., at that time, one Hero Honda CD 100 bearing No.KA.11/J 5637 being driven by its rider in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the bicycle on its back portion.
Due to impact, minor claimant and his father fell down and minor claimant sustained fracture to his right leg and other injuries on the parts of the body.
3. Heard the argument from both sides and perused the records.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company submitted that, in the present case, the accident was not occurred and more over, the alleged vehicle in question was not involved in the accident, as there is no complaint, FIR and other evidences, except the wound certificate and self-explanatory evidence of owner of the vehicle and eye witness.
Therefore, absolutely, there is no evidence to prove the factum of accident and also involvement of alleged vehicle.

Hence, submitted that the Tribunal has committed error only in believing the wound certificate and MLC extract and coming to wrong conclusion that the accident was caused and accordingly, awarded compensation.
Hence, submitted that, this approach of the Tribunal is not correct.
5. Further, submitted that there is no evidence that the hospital authorities have forwarded the Medico Legal Intimation report to the Police.
Therefore, the factum of accident and involvement of offending vehicle is not believable.
Further, submitted that as per Rule-232 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules enclosure of FIR and other documents are necessary, but they have not been appended to the claim petition.
Therefore, submitted that only on the basis of oral evidence of the owner and eye- witness, the factum of accident is not proved.
Further, submitted that P.W.2, even though, is stated to be eye- witness, but he is the planted witness.
Further, submitted that the accident was caused on 16.12.2011, but the claim petition was filed only on 23.12.2013 before the Tribunal.
Therefore, for this gap of two years, there was no effort made by the claimant either to approach the Police or the Tribunal.
Therefore, submitted that, absolutely, there is no minimum evidence on the part of the claimant to prove the factum of accident and involvement of alleged offending vehicle.
Hence, prays to set aside the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal by allowing the appeal.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.1 submitted that the owner of motor cycle had admitted the accident and also P.W.2 who is eye- witness has deposed before the Court that he witnessed the accident and admitted the injured to the hospital.
Therefore, submitted that these evidences are sufficient to prove that the accident was occurred.
Further, submitted that the Wound Certificate and MLC extract are sufficient to prove the factum of accident and the claimant had sustained injuries.
Therefore, the Tribunal by appreciating all the evidences on record has correctly assessed the evidence and came to the conclusion that the rider of the motor cycle was rash and negligent.
Accordingly, the Tribunal has granted compensation, which is just and proper.

Hence,
prays to dismiss the appeal.

7. In the present case, the accident was caused on 16.12.2013, as per the claimant the rider of Hero Honda Motor Cycle bearing No.KA.11/J 5637, dashed the claimant and caused the accident and in the said accident the claimant sustained injuries.
When this being the fact the claimant has not lodged the complaint before the Police only two documents are produced viz., which are the Wound Certificate marked as Exhibit-P1 and MLC, Exhibit- P2.
Except these evidence, there are no other documentary evidence to show that there was accident and also involvement of the Hero Honda Motor Cycle bearing No.KA.11/J 5637 above stated.
8. PW-2 is stated to be an eye-witness but his evidence does not have any corroboration and utmost the evidence of PW-2 is found to be self-explanatory.
The father of the claimant is examined as PW-1.
But there is no explanation why complaint is not given and the FIR was not registered.

sentences.text: After lapse of two years as on the date of the accident, for the very first time before the Statutory Authorities claim petition was put forward narrating the accident and involvement of the vehicle, sustaining injuries in the said accident.
Therefore, there is no believable evidence proving the factum of the accident and involvement of the vehicle.

But respondent No.2 is owner and the insurance policy holder of offending Hero Honda Motor Cycle bearing No.KA.11/J-5637 has stated that there was an accident and the aforesaid vehicle was involved in the accident.
Respondent No.2 quite naturally said so because there is insurance policy.
If there was no insurance policy then the owner might not have said the said statement.

Therefore,
there is no minimum evidence to believe that Hero Honda Motor Cycle bearing No.KA.11/J 5637 was involved in the said accident.
9. Exhibit-P1 is the Wound Certificate issued by Sanjo Hospital, Srinivasapura, Mandya in which it is only stated that there was a road traffic accident.
Exhibit-P2 is the MLC Extract of the hospital.
In which it is stated that the claimant was hit by the motor cycle, but this alone cannot prove the factum of accident and involvement of the motor cycle.
10. Furthermore, regarding the accident, for the first time the claim petition is filed after two years from the date of the accident.

Even though there is no limitation of time to file claim petition before the Tribunal, but in the absence of any police documents regarding occurrence of accident, such huge delay can be fatal regarding factum of the accident.

11. As per Rule-232(c) of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules reads as follows:
"(c) move application before the concerned registering authority in Form 63-A and gather information about the motor vehicle(s) involved, and the driving license(s)
held by the driver(s) thereof as per details mentioned in Form 63-B;"
12.
Even though the words used in the aforesaid Section cannot be construed as a mandatory, even atleast it can be taken a suggestive in nature.
But a piece of evidence is necessary to prove the factum of accident and the involvement of the vehicle on all its preponderance of probabilities.

Therefore,
this creates doubt in the mind as to whether the accident occurred? and whether there was involvement of the vehicle in the accident?

Also one more thing is to be considered on the above reasoning regarding the claim petition that even though it may be assumed that the claimant had suffered injuries in the accident, but the involvement of the offending vehicle is not proved?
The appellant is made as a party because insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.
Respondent No.2 has admitted that his vehicle has caused injury in the accident.
Therefore, upon considering the evidence on record, there is no even a minute evidence to believe that the Hero Honda Motor Cycle bearing No.KA.11/J 5637 was involved in the accident.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the claimant relied on the judgment of this Court in the case of MEENAKSHAMMA vs. HANUMANTHAPPA1 and submitted that non-registration of criminal case is not an adverse factor to show that the accident has not occurred.

No doubt mere non-registration of criminal case is not a ILR 1996 KAR 161 - 11 - ground to deny the case, but there shall be some minimum evidence to prove the factum of the accident and the involvement of the alleged offending vehicle.
Also failure to produce MLC intimation and report of police is also not a ground to deny the claim.
But there should be some minimum evidence to prove the factum of accident and involvement of the vehicle.
15. These are two important ingredients to prove the accident in any claim petition.
Even though the claim petition filed is under the Motor Vehicles Act, it can be even considered under some other Act.
But minimum evidence is warranted.

Considering the case on all its preponderance of probabilities,
atleast to have a say, some evidence has to be placed to believe the factum of the accident.
If there is no minimum piece of evidence, to believe the factum of accident, then it can be said that the factum of accident is not proved.
To disbelieve the facts narrated in the claim petition, one more strong suspicion is that there is two years delay in filing the claim petition.

Just because there is a delay in filing claim petition,
ipso-facto is not a ground to deny the claim petition.
But in the facts and circumstances involved and in the absence of evidence regarding factum for proving the accident that plays significant role in getting suspicious regarding the claim made.
17. The respondent No.2 - owner and policy-holder has stated that his Hero Honda Motor Cycle was involved in the accident.
It is borne out from the record that since there were damages to the said motor cycle, therefore he has admitted that his motor cycle was involved in the accident.

Anyhow,
the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation, this is the attitude shown by the respondent No.2-owner from seeing the evidence on record.
As per Section-134(c) of M.V. Act it is the duty cast on the driver or the owner of the vehicle to give information / intimation regarding accident to the insurance company and all other particulars.
But there is no evidence to show that respondent No.2 has informed the insurance company in compliance with Section-134(c) of M.V. Act.

Even though non-compliance of this duty on the part of the owner cannot be made a ground to reject claim petition, but in the given facts and circumstances involved in the accident, if the owner has given information regarding the accident to the insurance company, then the factum of accident and involvement of vehicle in question would have been probablised.
But the owner has not complied with the provisions of Section- 134(c) of M.V. Act.

Therefore, at the initial point of time if information was given to the insurance company that such The Branch Manager vs Sri. Manoj G.N on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89130324/
5 accident was occurred and the alleged vehicle was involved in the accident and even though the complaint is not lodged before the Police and there is no registration of criminal case, then the proving of accident and - 14 - involvement of vehicle

19. Therefore, even though the medical records at Exhibits-P1 and P2 and Exhibits-C1 to C6 medical records show that the claimant had sustained injuries in the accident, but regarding the proof of involvement of the Hero Honda CD 100 bearing No.KA.11/J 5637, there is absolutely no evidence.

Even though there is no minimum evidence is available to prove that the vehicle was involved in the accident however, respondent No.2 has admitted that his motor cycle was involved in the accident,
then he shall pay the compensation to the claimant, but not the appellant - insurance company.
20. This Court has ordered that the appellant - insurance company to deposit the entire award amount and the claimant has withdrawn the said amount.

Therefore, the claimant has to repay/refund the said - 15 - amount to the insurance company and then recover the amount from respondent No.2 - Hanumanthappa owner of Hero Honda CD 100 bearing No.KA.11/J 5637.
Therefore, the burden is put on the respondent Nos.2 and 3 to pay the compensation to the claimant.
In this regard the appeal succeeds.

Hence, I pass the following order:
ORDER i) The appeal is Allowed.
ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 21.07.2015 in MVC.No.1477/2013 passed by Addl. Senior Civil Judge & CJM, and MACT, Mandya is modified to the extent and that the appellant insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
But respondent Nos.2 and 3 shall pay the compensation to the claimant.

iii) The claimant shall repay/refund the compensation amount to the insurance company and then recover the amount from respondent No.2 - Hanumanthappa owner of Hero Honda CD 100 - 16 - bearing No.KA.11/J 5637.
Respondent Nos.2 and 3 to pay the compensation to the claimant in this regard.
